A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neural network approach can be considered as a powerful tool to retrieve refractivity and temperature profiles in the inter-tropical ocean area from FORMOSAT-5/COSMIC GPS occultation data.

the proposed neural network approach can be used to retrieve refractivity profiles with an RMS of 1.5 % in the troposphere and 1.0 % in the stratosphere, and dry pressure profiles with an RMS error of 1.0 hPa in the troposphere, 2.0 hPa in stratosphere and 0.1 hPa in the mesosphere.

the proposed method is able to provide refractivity, temperature and pressure profiles with an accuracy comparable to that of the ECMWF data, while the retrieved humidity profiles are in good agreement with ECMWF data in the tropics and in the mid-latitudes.

the proposed neural networks are able to retrieve the dry refractivity, temperature and pressure profiles, as well as the wet refractivity and humidity profiles, with a good accuracy.

the neural network approach is able to retrieve the atmospheric parameters with a good accuracy, even in a region of the globe where the density of the available GPS radio occultation measurements is low.
